articles.title: Woodside's Louisiana LNG to Supply QatarEnergy for 20 Years
articles.description: QatarEnergy has placed a 20-year order for up to three million metric tons per annum of liquefied natural gas from Woodside's under-construction project on the United States Gulf Coast.

articles.title: North America Enters Rig Addition Streak, BH Shows
articles.description: North America added six rigs week on week, according to Baker Hughes' latest North America rotary rig count.

articles.title: Oil Market Weighs Next Stage in Iran Conflict After Midterms
articles.description: A 'massive blue wave mid-term election result' saw the Democrats take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, Saxo Bank highlighted.

articles.title: TotalEnergies Bags 15-Year Deal to Supply LNG to China's Jiangsu
articles.description: Jiangsu Guoxin awarded TotalEnergies a 15-year contract to supply 900,000 metric tons per year of liquefied natural gas to the Chinese province for city gas supply and flexible power generation.

articles.title: Oil climbs amid US midterm results and Middle East tensions
articles.description: Oil prices increased on Wednesday 4 November as investors monitored developments following the US midterm elections, which resulted in Democrats securing majorities in both houses of Congress.

articles.title: Energy Transfer sanctions $1.6bn South Mississippi pipeline project
articles.description: Energy Transfer has approved a final investment decision (FID) for the $1.6bn South Mississippi Pipeline Project in southern Mississippi, US.

articles.title: US Oil Inventories Fall Further As Demand Holds
articles.description: Crude oil inventories in the United States saw a decrease of 900,000 barrels during the week ending October 30, according to new data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) released on Wednesday. The decrease brings commercial stockpiles to 409.8 million barrels, according to government data, which is now 4% below the five-year average for this time of year. Total commercial petroleum inventories slipped by 8.2 million barrels during the reporting period. The EIA’s data release follows API’s figures that were released…

articles.title: Brent Falls to $100 as Traders Bet on a U.S.-Iran Deal
articles.description: Oil traders are pricing a U.S.-Iran settlement and discounting the threats around it. As of 9:40 a.m. ET on Wednesday, Brent had fallen $3.04, or 2.9%, to $100.60 per barrel, its third straight loss, and WTI had dropped $2.86, or 3%, to $93.23. Murban slipped $1.27 to $100.90. Both crude benchmarks traded higher early before reversing in a volatile session. President Trump told the Financial Times that Washington has no immediate plans to strike Iran. “We seem to be getting everything we want,” he said. Vice President JD Vance said…

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine Head to White House for Melania Trump-Led Talks
articles.description: US first lady Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on November 5, with both sides confirming their participation in a meeting focused on a localized cease-fire in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, as a new round of US-mediated peace talks is set to take place next week. The meeting follows a six-day cease-fire in and around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, which Melania Trump said she helped broker to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and the evacuation of vulnerable civilians. articles.title: UAE-Controlled Moeve Sells Algerian Upstream Assets
articles.description: Spanish energy firm Moeve has agreed to sell its upstream oil and gas assets in Algeria to units of Indonesia’s state energy firm Pertamina in a deal that sees Moeve, majority owned by Abu Dhabi’s fund Mubadala, exiting the upstream business globally. Moeve, which rebranded from Cepsa in 2024 “to drive the energy transition towards a more sustainable future,” is nearly 62% owned by Mubadala, the sovereign investment company of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Moeve is selling its entire interests in the non-operated…

articles.title: Lone Star Goes Blue
articles.description: Democrats swept the governor's office, a U.S. Senate seat and a host of down-ballot slots in the midterm election, a rejection of the Republican party and President Donald Trump.

articles.title: Democrats Win Texas Oil Regulator Seat for First Time Since 1990
articles.description: Texas voters on Tuesday elected a Democrat to the Railroad Commission, the regulator of the state’s oil and gas industry, for the first time since 1990. They also elected a Democratic governor who promised to halt new data center construction. Democrats running against data centers took the governorships of Georgia and Ohio and won control of Georgia’s utility regulator. Voters cast those ballots with gasoline at its highest Election Day price on record. State Rep. Jon Rosenthal, a former oilfield engineer who calls himself a “drill…

articles.title: European Gas Prices Fall 2% as Traders Wait on Trump’s Next Move in Iran
articles.description: European benchmark natural gas prices fell in the early morning on Wednesday, as traders brace for what will happen next in Iran after U.S. President Donald Trump lost Republican control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections on Tuesday. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, fell by 2% as of 9 a.m. in Amsterdam on Wednesday, erasing earlier gains of about 1%, as the market remains anxious about Trump’s next moves on Iran. articles.title: CVR Energy to acquire two US refineries from Marathon for $4.2bn
articles.description: CVR Energy to acquire two US refineries and associated marketing assets from Marathon Petroleum for about $4.2bn plus net working capital.

articles.title: Nigeria's Oil and Gas Output Rises to 3.04 Million Boepd
articles.description: Nigeria’s NNPC raised its oil and gas production in September from a month earlier as output was restarted at some oilfields, the state-owned oil and gas company said in its latest monthly report this week. NNPC’s total oil and gas production rose to 3.04 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), up from 3.01 million boepd in the previous month, amid slightly higher crude oil and natural gas production and flat condensate output, NNPC’s report showed. Revenues came in at $3.4 billion (4.608 trillion Nigerian naira), in…

articles.title: Renewables Stocks Soar as Democrats Sweep U.S. Congress
articles.description: Renewable energy stocks rallied in Asia and Europe on Wednesday as Tuesday’s mid-term elections in the United States resulted in a sweeping victory for the Democrats, who took control of both the House and Senate. The “blue wave” of the elections turned into a “blue trade” in equity markets, where renewable energy stocks soared at opening in many Asian and European markets. Investors are betting that Democrats would favor renewable energy, unlike President Donald Trump, who has been openly hostile to clean energy in…

articles.title: Iran Says Four Oil Tankers Destroyed by Mines Near Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: Four oil tankers were destroyed after hitting naval mines in an area south of the Strait of Hormuz proscribed by Iran as prohibited for navigation, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Wednesday, as attacks on vessels in the region intensify while crude oil flows have dipped from recent highs. The four tankers are still ablaze, while two other vessels have been seized, the Revolutionary Guards said. While flows have recovered substantially from the lows in the spring, the security situation in and near the Strait of Hormuz…

articles.title: India Races to Triple Coal Stockpiles to Prevent Summer Blackouts
articles.description: India’s coal, power, and railway ministries are working jointly to boost the country’s stocks of coal ahead of next summer, Bloomberg has reported, citing unnamed sources. The target total is 55 million tons—a substantial boost from the current inventory, which amounts to 18 million tons. The targeted amount should be secured by the end of the current Indian fiscal year, March 31. Currently, coal stocks are at their lowest since 2021, Bloomberg noted in its report. The amount in stock is only enough for six days of power generation…

articles.title: China Now Home to Nearly Half of World's Clean Industrial Plants
articles.description: China is home to 49% of the world’s “clean industrial plants” thanks to massive investments in energy transition projects, solidifying its position as the biggest investor in wind, solar, batteries, and other alternative energy sources. According to a report by decarbonization outlet the Mission Possible Partnership, China accounted for $45 billion in energy transition investments this year. The number of “clean industrial plants: above includes both facilities already in operation and facilities under construction, Reuters…

articles.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Middle East Supply Fears Return
articles.description: Crude oil prices, which fell to their lowest in four weeks, staged a rebound earlier today, as traders shifted their attention from the U.S. midterms to the Middle East, awaiting the next step in the war. Benchmarks dropped sharply on Tuesday on reports that Iran may be open to discussions on previously non-negotiable issues, but at the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $103.60 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $95.98 per barrel, after two energy consultancies warned against too much Gulf oil supply rebound optimism. articles.title: Oil Prices Swing on Conflicting Iran Signals
articles.description: Oil markets remain volatile as traders weigh Iran war risks against improving regional supply.

articles.title: Pentagon Eyes Unprecedented 75-Year Deal to End China's Rare Earth Stranglehold
articles.description: The U.S. Army wants first dibs on American-produced heavy rare earths, and REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) has just signed a landmark nonbinding term sheet that could put it at the top of the military's supply chain list. And the terms are extraordinary. The term sheet proposes a potential 75-year operating lease on approximately 200 acres at Tooele Army Depot in Utah, where REalloys would build and operate a facility processing dysprosium and terbium, two metals China has spent decades monopolizing. articles.title: Iran War Doubles Egypt’s LNG Bill as Gas Output Keeps Falling
articles.description: The war on Iran has doubled what Egypt pays for imported LNG, and Cairo is deferring cargoes into 2027 and burning fuel oil in its power plants to hold down the bill. Egypt’s own output fell to 3.63 bcf/d in August as older fields declined faster than new wells came online, and the petroleum ministry has now extended the deadline for bids on 14 exploration blocks meant to reverse that decline to December 14 after companies asked for more time. articles.title: Global Diesel Crunch Set to Last Well Into 2027
articles.description: While crude oil imports in Asia have reached pre-war levels, imports of refined products remain weak as gasoline and diesel imports from the Middle East have crashed amid reduced refining capacity.
